name: Reading for Understanding (Comprehension)

objectives.text: Retell the main events of a Bible story in the correct order
Identify the main characters and the setting of a Bible story
Ask questions about words or ideas in a Bible passage that are hard to understand
Answer who, what, when, and where questions about a passage using details from the text
Explain the plain meaning of a short passage in your own words without adding to it
Classify a passage as narrative, poetry, law, prophecy, gospel, or letter using clues in the text
Support each statement about what a passage means with specific words or details from the text
Use clues in the surrounding verses to determine the meaning of an unfamiliar word or phrase
Compare two Bible stories to find similarities in how God acts toward his people
Explain how the beginning, conflict, and resolution of a biblical narrative reveal its point
Determine the author's main point in a passage and identify the details that support it
Explain how figurative language and parallelism in biblical poetry convey meaning
Explain the tradition's teaching that the things necessary for salvation are so clearly set forth in Scripture that ordinary readers can understand them by due use of ordinary means
Interpret the meaning of key words within their immediate context
Explain how a passage fits within the flow of its chapter and book
Apply the Reformed principle that Scripture interprets Scripture by using a clearer passage to clarify a harder one
Use historical and cultural background information to clarify the meaning of a passage
Explain how Jesus taught that the Old Testament Scriptures speak of him
Explain the tradition's teaching on how the Spirit's illumination and diligent study work together in understanding Scripture
Trace the logical flow of an argument in an epistle by analyzing connecting words such as therefore, because, and so that
Construct a detailed outline of a biblical book that shows its structure and major sections
Perform an independent word study to clarify the meaning of a crucial term across its uses
Evaluate competing interpretations of a passage using textual evidence and context
Write a summary of a passage that accurately reflects the author's intent and argument

changes: Kept and reworded the real comprehension skills (retelling, characters, questioning, plain meaning, genre, main point, context, word meaning, argument flow, outlining, word study, summary). Dropped the grade 3 picture retelling as a duplicate of the kindergarten objective and folded observation versus interpretation into a text-evidence objective to avoid overlap with Inductive Bible Study. Added context clues, narrative structure, biblical poetry, background information, Scripture interpreting Scripture, clarity of Scripture, illumination and study, Christ in the Old Testament, and evaluating interpretations. Anchored confessional objectives to Westminster Confession of Faith 1.6, 1.7, and 1.9 and replaced bare references with verse ranges.
